The shared bounded parser detects comma, semicolon, tab and pipe outside quoted fields, honors sep=, and preserves escaped quotes, multiline values, trailing empty cells and leading zeros. Manual separator selection also supports colon; headers can be disabled. Source text remains available through the formatted-preview toggle. Local and remote text previews use the same parser; encoding follows the preview selector/BOM. Limits: 128 KiB source, 2,000 records, 128 columns, 100,000 cells, 16,384 characters per cell. Truncation is reported; unfinished final records are omitted.

Media converter layout: Conversion settings and Advanced are separate tabs without a nested settings ScrollViewer. Destination and parallelism remain below both tabs. Queue column widths are recomputed from the grid width, reserving vertical scrollbar space; long text uses ellipsis and tooltips. Column dragging is disabled to keep the last column visible.

Illustrated native help

F1 opens context-sensitive native help with 44 linked topics in Czech or English. Numbered screenshots explain real controls using generated demonstration files. Click an illustration for native zoom (slider, scroll, Escape to close); no browser or internet is needed. Other interface languages show the English article language explicitly. Figures are embedded resources under source/help/images and accept curated identifiers only, never file paths or external URLs.

Linux disks (read-only)

Connections → Linux disks opens a native ext2/3/4 browser for physical USB disks without Windows drive letters and raw images. Select source, scan MBR/GPT partitions, select a filesystem, navigate with Enter/Backspace, preview with F3 or copy out with F5. Administrator access may be needed for raw physical disks; the reader has an explicit elevation button. Sources are opened read-only; dirty or unsupported filesystems are rejected. LUKS, LVM, RAID, Btrfs and ZFS are not supported. Export uses a new folder and refuses the source physical disk; symbolic links and special files are skipped. See F1 → Linux disks for limits and collision handling.

Only confirmed removable USB drives receive native safe-removal and Windows format commands on right-click. System/application disks are excluded. No native eject or formatting action is exercised by automated tests.

Flash drive actions

Removable drives use the native Windows removable-drive icon in the drive bar and selector. Right-click a drive to safely remove its physical USB device or open the Windows Format dialog for its exact letter. The system and application disks are protected, including shared removable-parent ancestry. Operations are revalidated against device identity before invoking Windows. Active file operations disable these commands. Affected panels leave the disk and their watchers/previews are released; safe removal handles all drive letters of that physical disk. Failure leaves Windows in control and reports the veto, without forced dismount or process termination.

Internal editor and analyzer expansion

F4 opens local text/source files in the tabbed AvalonEdit editor by default; a setting retains the external-editor workflow. The menu, context menu and Shift+F4 provide explicit external editing. JSON formatting preserves exact numeric lexemes and rejects duplicate keys. YAML is syntax-checked with YamlDotNet without alias expansion; XML prohibits DTD/external entities. The editor supports indentation guides, JSON/YAML folding, search, next replacement, line navigation, encoding/BOM and EOL preservation. Complete documents are limited to 16 MiB. Saves reject concurrent external changes and use a flushed adjacent temporary file. Closing modified documents or the main window prompts for save/discard/cancel. Remote/archive editors retain their established working-copy commit workflows.

The analyzer adds treemaps, per-row share bars/percentages (whole scan or parent), context actions across charts/tree/results, recycling UI virtualization, multiple roots with overlap deduplication, verified empty-folder candidates, and current-path/progress/error diagnostics. Treemaps show up to 512 individual child folders and 1024 direct files, with exact remainder groups and matching-file selection. Multiple roots retain independent totals and combined indexes/snapshots. Cancelling blocked OS reads waits for the call to return; retry starts only after the previous scan exits.

Batch rename retains stable row containers across previews, disables Start while a new calculation is pending or invalid, and persists ten recent values independently for name/find/replacement. Token menus open on Alt alone or Alt+Down, without opening on ordinary mouse clicks. SMB enumeration uses independent workers and a 15-second UI timeout; late reads cannot overwrite newer results. Watcher shutdown and creation run away from the UI. Icon cache locks never surround filesystem or shell I/O.

Editor menus and audio tempo

The internal editor uses File/Edit/View/Tools/Help menus instead of a command-button strip. Syntax, encoding and line endings are in the format bar and are retained per document. The active filename sits at the right of the title; single-document editing hides the redundant tab row. New text defaults to UTF-8 without BOM and Windows CRLF. View exposes line wrapping, line numbers, whitespace and indentation. File keeps save/conflict/unsaved-close guards.

Audio conversion has a separate Speed and duration settings tab. Defaults preserve pitch using atempo; an alternative uses asetrate plus resampling to change both speed and pitch. Presets include exact 24000/1001 film ratios and 50/75/125/150/200 percent, custom 10–1000 percent, and target duration per file. Duration accepts hours/minutes/seconds and milliseconds. Target mode aligns the final PCM duration with end trimming/padding; compressed encoders may introduce frame padding. Conversion progress and output-duration checks use the changed duration. Stream copy and unchanged video timing are rejected with active tempo changes. Timed chapters are omitted rather than copied with invalid timestamps. No additional runtime library is required.

External application dispatch and transfer units

F4 uses an explicit internal-text/source allowlist. Office/PDF and other non-text types open through the default Windows Open association, not the optional Edit verb. Shift+F4 invokes the external application directly from the main window or current editor document. Executables and scripts retain data-only text editing. Copy progress, background summaries and transfer graphs label their existing binary conversion correctly as MiB/s; byte counters, rate timing and the copy engine are unchanged.

External editing explicitly routes CSV to Microsoft Excel (App Paths, XLSX executable association or standard Office install paths) and HTML/HTM to Windows Notepad. It does not change system associations. Missing Excel reports an actionable error. The external-edit toolbar icon is removed; menu/context commands and Shift+F4 remain. Plain internal F4 editing is unchanged for CSV/HTML.

Missing or broken Windows associations for external editing now show the native owned Open with dialog, including XLS with no default application. Users can opt into a permanent association when Windows offers it; cancellation is not an error. Explicit CSV-to-Excel and HTML-to-Notepad routes remain unchanged.

Current processing and layout

The analyzer waits for Start so scope and minimum-size filters can be configured first. Chart type selection is above the chart; result and chart panes have priority over options. SMART cards distinguish detected HDD, SSD and NVMe types, with unknown types retained explicitly. Supported tools dock via Background and restore via Detail.

Image conversion uses the matched Magick.NET Q8 OpenMP x64 15.0.0 package. Whole-file workers share a CPU thread budget; codec limits still apply. Audio workers process separate whole files with FFmpeg. Parallelism above the logical CPU count is permitted, but does not guarantee acceleration. Progress percentages have a dedicated column. Queue ETA uses source duration (audio) or image work estimates, observed throughput and the parallel schedule; it warms up and remains an estimate. Final verification/commit is a distinct finishing phase. Some MP3 metadata duration estimates can currently cause false duration-check rejection.

Title: Archives and archivers
Summary: Detailed workflows for the current interface with updated screenshots.
Body:
Archives and optional archivers

File Compass browses archives as folders and uses the bundled 7-Zip engine for supported formats. ZIP, 7z, TAR/GZ and supported external RAR/ARJ/LHA creation are available according to the selected format/tool. Existing ARJ/LHA/TAR archives have read-only limitations. Archive operations enforce path, entry-count, memory, elapsed-time, expanded-size, free-space and nesting limits configurable in Settings → Archives. Passwords remain outside worker command-line arguments.

Compression progress shows the current file, operation completion and compression-ratio history. The chart's horizontal axis is operation completion (0–100%); the vertical axis is output/input percentage and can exceed 100%. The connected samples show how the ratio changes during the operation. See operations (OPERATIONS.md) for verified move-to-archive and split ZIP/7z volumes.

Obtain optional tools

Settings → Archives can find an existing installation, select an EXE, or open Get add-on / Get WinRAR/RAR. Download begins only in the separate download window. Existing configured/common/PATH installations are used without downloading.

ARJ32 and LHa are prepared under plugins/archivers beside the program, without modifying Windows or Program Files. The window is modeless and supports cancellation. Completion saves the path; manually configured paths remain supported.

WinRAR uses RARLAB's original installer. After downloading, choose Run installer and complete its normal installation steps. File Compass does not run it automatically, install silently or redistribute a standalone Rar.exe. It subsequently searches for the installation; use Find WinRAR if installation is still running.

Sources and licenses

• WinRAR/RAR 7.23 x64: https://www.rarlab.com/download.htm ; EULA https://www.rarlab.com/license.htm . Trial software, up to 40 days without buying a license. Downloading does not include a license.

• ARJ32 3.31: https://arj32.com/ . Shareware under ARJ Software's supplied terms. The original ZIP/nested SFX are extracted only; SFX installation/test commands are not executed. Original license/documentation files are retained.

• LHa 1.14i, GnuWin32: https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/lha.htm . The original distribution and documentation are retained. This is the LHa compressor, not the Lhasa extractor.

RAR/ARJ/LHA creation runs external processes without passwords in arguments. Legacy ARJ/LHA filename-encoding limitations still apply.

Integrity and maintenance

Downloads use certificate-validated HTTPS, a 128 MiB maximum and time limits. Pinned versions, URLs and SHA-256 package/EXE hashes are in ArchivePluginInstaller.cs. ARJ is verified before its nested SFX is opened; WinRAR installers also require Authenticode verification before publication and execution. Changed upstream content is rejected.

ARJ/LHA extraction uses the bundled verified codec in an isolated worker with normal archive/path limits. Prepared directories are published atomically; cancelled/failed downloads do not activate a tool. Managed archivers are verified and held open before execution. User-managed installations outside the add-on store use the chosen path.

There is no automatic search for the latest EXE or automatic update. A new managed release requires updated pinned metadata, license/package review and integration tests. A newer personal installation can be selected manually.

Compression quality is passed to the native codec for both ordinary and encrypted ZIP. ZIP no longer collapses all higher settings into the same .NET Optimal setting. The 0–9 choice maps to each codec's supported quality steps: native 7-Zip stages for ZIP/7z/GZip/BZip2/XZ, RAR methods 0–5, and ARJ methods 0–4 (where method 1 is strongest). TAR has no compression; the supported LHA tool exposes a fixed method, so their quality control is disabled and explained. Changing a level does not guarantee a different size for every payload, especially data already compressed.

When a source cannot be opened or read during folder preparation, a clean prompt offers Retry, Skip or Stop. Skip excludes that file, removes any partial staging copy and reports omitted paths after the operation. Stop preserves an existing destination archive. Move-to-archive keeps skipped source files and their containing directories; only included files that passed verification are deleted. If every directly selected file is skipped, no empty replacement is published.

Compression levels and unreadable inputs

The selected level is mapped to each supported archiver rather than ignored by ZIP. Higher levels may produce identical sizes for small, incompressible or already compressed files; TAR stores data without compression. File preparation shows counts and names without percentage bars. Compression then shows blue total/current-file progress. Locked/unreadable inputs offer retry, skip, skip-all and cancellation where supported; skipped inputs remain at their original locations during move-to-archive.

Self-extracting archives (SFX)

In the creation dialog choose More → Tools → Self-extracting archive. The output changes to .exe, and the basic page summary opens that option directly. Creation never executes the generated EXE.

| Payload | Required module/tool | Supported combinations | | --- | --- | --- | | 7z | Bundled, integrity-checked 7z.sfx | Password, move after verification, separate archives, split volumes | | ZIP | Configured WinRAR.exe and Zip.SFX beside it | Password, move after verification, separate archives; single volume | | RAR | Configured RAR/WinRAR and Default.SFX beside it | Move after verification, separate archives; single volume | | ARJ | Configured ARJ32 with its embedded Win32 module | Move after verification, separate archives; single volume |

For split 7z, keep the launcher name.exe and every name.7z.001, name.7z.002, … together. Do not split the completed EXE as arbitrary file fragments. LHA and TAR/GZ do not expose SFX with the supported tools. Existing SFX containers are read-only in archive browsing.

ZIP/RAR/ARJ modules belong to their external archivers and are not redistributed with File Compass. Their license terms apply. In particular ARJ Software's supplied SFX.TXT requires a separate distribution license for non-personal distribution of ARJ/ARJ32 self-extracting archives; a standard registration is not sufficient. The bundled 7-Zip license remains included with its module.

The archive payload and resulting EXE are verified before publication; move-to-archive retains its existing source hash verification. Passwords stay in the isolated codec worker and are not put in external-tool arguments. Integration checks really run generated text-only 7z/ZIP/RAR/ARJ SFX fixtures and a split-7z launcher, and verify the extracted bytes.

Title: Cloud accounts, authorization and transfers
Summary: Detailed workflows for the current interface with updated screenshots.
Body:
Cloud storage: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and iCloud Drive

New Google sign-ins use File Compass's publisher desktop OAuth configuration, config/oauth/google.json. Each user signs in with their own account without entering Client ID/Secret. Without publisher configuration, new Google sign-in is unavailable with an explanation. Existing accounts retain their old authorization identity until explicitly signed in again.

Google registration status

As of 23 October 2026, the external OAuth app is in production but not verified, requesting https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive. Search Console website ownership is verified; Google branding verification still awaits propagation (Google requests a 24-hour wait before retrying). Restricted-scope review follows verified/published branding. An unverified-app warning and the 100-user project cap remain. Production status alone is not Google approval.

Website (https://rathousky-pro.github.io/file-compass-web/) · Privacy Policy (https://rathousky-pro.github.io/file-compass-web/privacy.html). Full Drive access enables management of existing folders, rather than only app-created files. Every user grants access separately and can revoke it. OneDrive/Dropbox do not use the Google client and are unaffected by Google's shared-client retirement.

Add an account

• Open Connections → Manage connections → Cloud storage, or the Connections toolbar button and Cloud storage tab.

• Choose Add account, the provider and a local display name.

• Choose Sign in in browser; select your account, complete MFA and review permissions on the provider's page.

• OneDrive may ask for a drive/library; work/school accounts may need administrator approval.

• When authorization succeeds, choose Connect.

Multiple accounts per provider are supported. Google/Microsoft/Dropbox passwords are entered only in the provider's browser page; authorization returns automatically. The app name may appear as rclone depending on provider/client; Google's File Compass branding is awaiting verification. Use Sign in again if authorization expires or is cancelled. Provider questions include explanatory wording and access to the original question.

Imported profiles

For accounts copied from another computer/Windows user, choose Sign in again. Authorization is independent of the original DPAPI key. A successful verified sign-in keeps the account name/identity and saves new local credentials; cancellation leaves the original profile unchanged. Other accounts/keys are unaffected.

The previous configuration remains in a protected .before-signin-… account backup. Remove account also removes these backups. Complete browser sign-in/MFA yourself.

Files

Cloud panels support browsing, Copy/F5, Move/F6, folders, rename and delete through the shared network queue; browsing can continue during transfers. Tabs/workspaces remember account identity without forcing startup sign-in.

Interrupted cloud uploads restart the current file; completed targets can be skipped. Editing/previews use temporary downloads and normal limits. Native Google documents can be exported on download where supported. Operations depend on service/account capabilities.

Cloud panels do not provide SSH terminals or direct metadata search. This version does not mount cloud storage as Explorer drive letters and requires neither WinFsp nor administrator installation for cloud access.

Disconnect, remove and revoke

Disconnect through Connections → Active connections or the connection-button context menu; saved authorization remains. Remove account deletes local configuration/tokens, not cloud files. Disconnect open panels and finish/remove pending transfers first. Revoke consent separately in Google/Microsoft/Dropbox account settings when required.

Local storage and protection

Accounts are in data/cloud; each has an encrypted rclone.conf and a key protected with Windows DPAPI for the current user. Copying the program does not transfer usable authorization to another user/computer. Cloud directories have restricted permissions. Tokens are not process arguments or user log output.

A hidden local helper provides SFTP on 127.0.0.1 only, with per-account passwords and pinned host keys. It is not accessible from the LAN and stops with File Compass.

iCloud Drive

Choose iCloud Drive when adding an account. Enter the Apple Account and its regular password in the native sign-in wizard, then the verification code from an Apple device. Enter sms at the device-code prompt to request SMS; select a trusted phone number if prompted. App-specific passwords are not supported. The password and backend authentication state are written only into the encrypted account configuration; they are not command-line arguments.

Enable Access iCloud Data on the Web in Apple settings and approve trusted-device access if requested, including with Advanced Data Protection. The bundled rclone 1.75.2 implements the Apple SRP/2FA and PCS approval flow. Sessions can require reauthentication after about 30 days; disconnect the account and use Log in again. Existing authorization remains intact if renewed sign-in is cancelled.

iCloud Drive uses the same account switching, panels, transfer queue and file operations as the other providers. iCloud Photos is not offered as a writable file account. Live Apple-account authorization and transfers require validation with an actual account; offline wizard tests do not establish live Apple compatibility.

Title: Third-party notices
Summary: Original license and third-party notice text.
Body:
Third-party notices

Paths below refer to the installation root unless a source path is stated. Original upstream license/copyright texts are retained with each component; this English inventory does not replace them.

libcurl 8.22.0 and libssh2 1.11.1

Network operations use the native FileCompassNetwork.dll adapter in plugins/network. It statically links libcurl (curl/MIT-like license), libssh2 (BSD-3-Clause) and dependencies from the official curl 8.22.0_3 Windows x64 package. libcurl handles FTP/FTPS; libssh2 handles SFTP/SCP/SSH. LibreSSL 4.3.3 supplies cryptography. Dependencies include zlib-ng, zstd, Brotli, libpsl, the public suffix list, nghttp2, nghttp3 and ngtcp2.

Original notices are in plugins/network/licenses; BUILD-MANIFEST.txt lists exact components/source links and the plugin manifest records package provenance/hashes. Static libraries/headers/original downloads are build-time inputs under source/downloads/network; adapter sources/build scripts are in source/native. No separate runtime installation is required. FluentFTP, SSH.NET and WinSCP are no longer runtime components.

Sources: https://curl.se/windows/ and https://libssh2.org/.

External SSHFS support

WinFsp — Windows File System Proxy, Copyright (C) Bill Zissimopoulos: https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp (GPLv3 with FLOSS exception; commercial licensing https://winfsp.dev/com/). SSHFS-Win: https://github.com/winfsp/sshfs-win ; component licenses/sources are listed in its License.txt/repository.

File Compass does not bundle these system components; it downloads unmodified official GitHub release installers only when requested.

7-Zip 26.04

Unmodified 7z.exe and 7z.dll are distributed in plugins/7zip without installation. Copyright (C) 1999–2026 Igor Pavlov. LGPL and additional terms are in plugins/7zip/License.txt. Corresponding sources: https://github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases/tag/26.04 and https://www.7-zip.org/download.html. File Compass uses a separate command-line process and the bundled codec. WinRAR is not bundled; users select their own installation.

WPF UI 4.3.0

WPF UI / WPF UI Abstractions (lepo.co), MIT. The .NET Framework 4.7.2 libraries run under File Compass's .NET Framework 4.8 target. Microsoft dependencies: System.Memory 4.6.3, System.Buffers 4.6.1, System.Numerics.Vectors 4.6.1 and System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 6.1.2 (MIT).

Libraries are in libraries, original notices in libraries/licenses. libraries/manifest.json records versions, official NuGet URLs and SHA-256. CompactMenu.xaml adapts WPF UI MenuItem for compact menus and retains its copyright notice. Other controls use library templates. Source: https://github.com/lepoco/wpfui/releases/tag/4.3.0.

SharpSevenZip

Managed wrapper: SharpSevenZip 2.0.128, LGPL-3.0-or-later. Source: https://github.com/JeremyAnsel/SharpSevenZip/tree/f4c16a6a95ace333fa33f38c1d69e44d77812eee Package: https://www.nuget.org/packages/SharpSevenZip/2.0.128 License and package metadata: libraries/licenses/SharpSevenZip. The wrapper is distributed as a separate unmodified DLL; it uses the existing bundled native 7z.dll. The pinned package and assembly hashes are in tools/fetch-archive-library.ps1 in the source distribution.

Microsoft Fluent UI System Icons

Copyright Microsoft Corporation. MIT license: libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-LICENSE.txt. Source: https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-system-icons Pinned revision: a347af95478f989038cccbf085978865264c048a (libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-SOURCE.json). Original SVG and PNG sources are in source/ui/icons. Runtime action icons are bundled in icons/Actions.*.fvicons. Title: CSV: tables, delimiters and encoding
Summary: CSV, TSV, TAB and PSV can be viewed as tables in F3 and Ctrl+Q quick preview. Preview never edits the file. Cell values remain text, so  00123  retains its leading zeros.   A demonstration inventory rendered as columns.
Body:
CSV, TSV, TAB and PSV can be viewed as tables in F3 and Ctrl+Q quick preview. Preview never edits the file. Cell values remain text, so 00123 retains its leading zeros.

Delimiter detection

Automatic detection compares records and favors consistent column counts. It honors a leading sep=; declaration. Quoted separators do not split cells, doubled quotes represent one literal quote, and values can span multiple physical lines. Spaces are not a universal delimiter: fixed-width text tables are not necessarily CSV.

Example and repair

The header Name;Price;Count followed by Cable;12,50;3 uses a semicolon, while the comma belongs to the price. Select Semicolon manually if detection is wrong. For a single giant column, check the delimiter first; for broken accents, change encoding in the top toolbar. These choices only rebuild the preview.

Large files and limits

The table reads the first 128 KiB, up to 2,000 records, 128 columns and approximately 100,000 cells. Extremely long cells are capped at 16,384 characters. An incomplete final record in a truncated excerpt is omitted to avoid misleading values. Check the status warning: visible row count is not necessarily the whole-file count. Disable Formatted preview to inspect original text. See viewer and encoding.

Title: Audio conversion, bitrate and VBR
Summary: Open Media → Convert audio. The dialog accepts audio and extracts a selected audio stream from supported video; it does not re-encode the video picture. Add files, check analysis and select an output folder.   Audio Conv
Body:
Current interface

Keep original format preserves each input container and codec when they can be written safely. Unchanged audio can be stream-copied; edits require re-encoding. An unsupported original format is an explicit error. Speed, duration and further options are in sidebar tabs revealed by More.

Quick image edits are part of the converter. Use the Size and rotation sidebar page for resizing and rotation; the mode, width, height and rotation controls stay on one row. Keep original format preserves each image format and extension, or each audio container and codec. Unchanged audio is stream-copied. Unsupported edits of an original codec report an error and leave the source intact.

Current workflow

Each worker converts one complete file using FFmpeg; codec/filter threads share a CPU budget. Output is checked before final commit, including codec, channels, sample rate and duration. Known limitation: some MP3 files have inaccurate metadata-based duration estimates and can be incorrectly rejected by duration verification. A validation failure does not by itself mean the encoder failed. The original input is retained.

Open Media → Convert audio. The dialog accepts audio and extracts a selected audio stream from supported video; it does not re-encode the video picture. Add files, check analysis and select an output folder.

CBR, ABR, VBR and CVBR

  • CBR uses a fixed bitrate for workflows or players requiring it.
  • ABR requests a target average. Actual rate can vary with duration and content; it does not guarantee an exact size for each file.
  • MP3 VBR uses quality 0–9, where 0 is best. There is no simultaneous binding target bitrate.
  • AAC and Vorbis quality-based VBR work in the other direction: higher values mean higher quality. Vorbis ranges from −1 to 10.
  • Opus VBR and CVBR have a target bitrate; CVBR constrains variation. Neither is identical to CBR.
  • FLAC, WAV and ALAC are lossless outputs. Increasing bit depth or converting MP3 to FLAC cannot restore information already lost.

Streams, channels and compatibility

The input-track setting selects an audio-stream ordinal, not a music metadata track number. That stream must exist in every selected batch input. Original channels preserves the source count; mono and stereo allow downmixing. Stereo to 5.1 requires explicit upmix. AC-3 and E-AC-3 support up to 5.1 here. Creating extra channels does not recover an original surround recording or produce Dolby Atmos.

Select a sample rate supported by the destination; for codec errors, try a supported value such as 48,000 Hz. WAV also supports 32-bit float; other supported lossless profiles use their available 16/24-bit settings.

Completion and cancellation

New outputs receive _converted and a number on collision. Originals are not overwritten. Completed outputs are verified and recorded in history. Cancel stops active conversions while retaining completed outputs; inspect other failures in the queue. Higher parallelism helps only when CPU, memory and disk throughput permit.

Continue to advanced options or undoing generated outputs.

Changing audio speed and duration

In Convert audio, open Speed and duration. Changes are applied while converting to a new file; the original is preserved.

The summary displays the selected item's source duration, output duration and calculated speed. The supported range is 10–1000%; values outside it are rejected before conversion. Extreme changes may create audible artifacts even when preserving pitch. Target-duration mode aligns the end after changing tempo by trimming or padding silence; lossy codecs may add frame padding.

Speed changes require encoding and cannot use Copy audio. Keep video is disabled because its timing would also need adjustment. Audio extracted from video can be processed separately. Timed chapters are not carried over when speed changes; ordinary text tags follow Keep metadata. All current audio output profiles, including multichannel outputs, use the same tempo processing.

Matching film versions requires the correct ratio and any initial offset. Equal duration alone cannot repair different cuts, missing scenes or different opening sequences.

Title: Advanced converter options
Summary: Advanced is a separate tab next to Conversion settings. Switching preserves values, queue, destination and parallelism; it starts nothing by itself. Neither tab contains an additional nested settings scrollbar.   Advance
Body:
Current interface

More reveals left navigation whose tabs replace settings in the main area. Images have Size and rotation; audio has its own speed and duration page. The queue and destination remain shared.

Advanced is a separate tab next to Conversion settings. Switching preserves values, queue, destination and parallelism; it starts nothing by itself. Neither tab contains an additional nested settings scrollbar.

Advanced image options

Metadata retention depends on the format. First frame only allows an animation to become a still image. Lossless WebP is available only for WebP; it cannot restore detail lost in an input JPEG. JPEG and BMP flatten transparency onto white. Choose supported GIF, WebP or TIFF when retaining multiple frames.

In compact windows explanatory paragraphs move to tooltips and help to leave controls and queue visible. Basic parameters are described under audio and images.

Title: Image conversion and batch resizing
Summary: Select images and open Media → Convert images. The queue can contain both images and audio; the media-type tab filters the relevant items. The selected settings apply to every checked input, while derived dimensions are
Body:
Current interface

The converter includes the former quick image edits. Keep original format preserves each input format independently. Size and rotation has its own sidebar tab. All landscape and All portrait rotate only oppositely oriented images: EXIF orientation is applied first, then rotation and resizing. A longest-edge limit of 1920 means a height of 1920 for portrait output. Originals are retained.

Quick image edits are part of the converter. Use the Size and rotation sidebar page for resizing and rotation; the mode, width, height and rotation controls stay on one row. Keep original format preserves each image format and extension, or each audio container and codec. Unchanged audio is stream-copied. Unsupported edits of an original codec report an error and leave the source intact.

Current workflow

Images use Magick.NET Q8 OpenMP x64. OpenMP can parallelize supported image operations; individual codecs have their own limits. Thread budgets are shared between concurrent files to avoid excessive oversubscription. This is not general GPU acceleration and not every operation uses all cores.

Select images and open Media → Convert images. The queue can contain both images and audio; the media-type tab filters the relevant items. The selected settings apply to every checked input, while derived dimensions are calculated separately for each image.

Choosing dimensions

  • Width only, 1280 px: each image becomes 1280 pixels wide and height follows its aspect ratio. This may also enlarge images.
  • Height only works in reverse. Dimensions account for orientation and rotation and are rounded to whole pixels.
  • Exact width × height forces both values. A different ratio distorts the image; this is not intelligent cropping.
  • Longest edge only reduces dimensions, useful for mixed portrait and landscape photos.
  • Percentage scales both sides proportionally. Fifty means half the width and half the height, not half the pixel count.

Formats and frames

PNG suits transparency and graphics; JPEG suits ordinary photos without transparency. JPEG and BMP flatten transparency onto white. For animations or multi-page inputs choose supported GIF/WebP/TIFF, or explicitly select First frame only under Advanced. GIF limits colors. Metadata and color information may not transfer identically between formats.

Outputs and failures

Originals are not overwritten. Outputs use _converted and a number on collision. Inspect each status: memory limits, damaged inputs and unsupported frame counts are separate failures. Reduce parallelism for very large photos. Completed outputs survive batch cancellation. Media also provides Simple image editing for adjustments without choosing a new format; its copies use a separate filename suffix.

See advanced options and metadata and renaming.

Title: Filenames and metadata in both directions
Summary: Media provides two opposite workflows. Rename using metadata builds filenames from fields already stored in a file. Metadata from file names parses the existing name and writes fields into the file. Confirm the direction
Body:
Media provides two opposite workflows. Rename using metadata builds filenames from fields already stored in a file. Metadata from file names parses the existing name and writes fields into the file. Confirm the direction before constructing a pattern: renaming alone does not repair missing tags.

Filename to metadata

The pattern must match the extension-free name and exact separators. For Artist - Album - 01 - Title.mp3, choose supported artist, album, track and title fields with the same spaces and hyphens. Insert exact token spellings from the menu; [Ignore] skips a segment. A field cannot repeat and adjacent fields require a literal separator.

Compare original and proposed values for every row before confirming. Unmatched names, invalid dates, unsupported fields and read-only files are not guessed around. Dates use yyyy-MM-dd or yyyyMMdd; times use HH-mm-ss or HHmmss. A time alone may be insufficient when no existing date is stored.

Metadata to filename

Available tokens also include filesystem creation, modification and access times, size and folder. For example [File.Created:yyyyMMdd_HHmmss] uses filesystem creation time, not automatically photo capture time. Choose an appropriate EXIF/Image field for photography and supported MP3 fields for music. Supply missing fields or choose another pattern; preview exposes empty or duplicate results.

Backups and limits

Metadata writes leave an original .filecompass-metadata-….bak beside the file. Keep it until checking the result. A batch supports up to 500 files and metadata writes support files up to 1 GB. Writable fields depend on the format; image and audio fields cannot be freely mixed. Cancellation retains completed writes and backups. See batch rename and history.

Title: Transaction history and safe undo
Summary: Selecting a transaction  The curved navigation-toolbar arrow opens history. You are not limited to the latest action: select a transaction and inspect its availability reason. Green means reversible, amber partially reve
Body:
History and undo

The curved toolbar arrow opens transaction history. Rows explain available, partially available and irreversible operations. Review details before undoing; a partial operation offers only available steps.

Copy, move or rename operations can have verified undo receipts. Identity and contents are rechecked; later edits, replacement files or unrelated folder contents may prevent undo. Overwriting and permanent deletion are not backups. Receipts are available in the current session; a persisted record alone does not guarantee undo after restarting.

Clear history

Transaction history and operation history offer Clear history with confirmation. It removes completed records and their undo receipts without changing actual files. Running and queued tasks remain. The control can be disabled during work or availability checks. Clearing is persisted, so removed records do not return after reloading.

Log

Operation history offers details, log export and, where available, retry or resume for interrupted tasks. Check paths and filenames before sharing a log.

Title: Locked files and using applications
Summary: If copying, renaming or deleting reports that a file is in use, open Which application is using this file. It lists processes Windows can report for that file, not every access on a remote server.   Check the process and
Body:
If copying, renaming or deleting reports that a file is in use, open Which application is using this file. It lists processes Windows can report for that file, not every access on a remote server.

  1. Check the process and its identity. Refresh if the application exited or restarted.
  2. Activate application switches to an available window; applications without a window cannot provide this action.
  3. Save your work in that application and close the file.
  4. Return to the operation and choose Retry, or Skip to continue without that file.

An empty list does not prove availability. The lock may have ended, belong to a network device or be unavailable from Windows. Repeatedly overwriting the destination does not resolve a source lock. See permissions and connectivity.

Title: Copy and move presets
Summary: A preset stores frequently reused operation-preparation settings, for example copying photos with preserved timestamps and verification. It is not an automatic scheduler or a permanent list of files to transfer.   Config
Body:
A preset stores frequently reused operation-preparation settings, for example copying photos with preserved timestamps and verification. It is not an automatic scheduler or a permanent list of files to transfer.

  1. Configure the copy or move dialog first and review its options.
  2. Save a clearly named preset. Confirm replacement only when intending to change an existing preset.
  3. On later use, load it and recheck destination, filter and collision handling.
  4. Start the operation separately. Loading a preset alone does not start it.

Up to 100 presets can be stored. A single-file destination preset is not automatically valid for multiple selected inputs. Presets cannot solve missing disks or disconnected services. See copy options.

Title: Linked panel browsing
Summary: Linked browsing keeps both panels in matching subfolders of two chosen roots. It helps inspect a working folder and a copy manually. It does not copy, compare contents or create missing folders.   Open matching local or
Body:
Linked browsing keeps both panels in matching subfolders of two chosen roots. It helps inspect a working folder and a copy manually. It does not copy, compare contents or create missing folders.

  1. Open matching local or mounted network folders, for example C:\Examples\Project and D:\Examples\Backup.
  2. Enable linked panel browsing. Current locations define the corresponding roots.
  3. Open a subfolder on one side; the other follows the relative path when it exists.
  4. Disable linking or redefine roots before freely browsing unrelated locations.

A missing counterpart is not an instruction to delete the other side. Use synchronization for an actual comparison and change plan. Check command availability for cloud and virtual locations.

Title: Command search and custom shortcuts
Summary: Find command searches available application actions by name. Use it when you know the intended task but not its menu location. Command availability still depends on the active panel and selection.   Open Find command and
Body:
Find command searches available application actions by name. Use it when you know the intended task but not its menu location. Command availability still depends on the active panel and selection.

  1. Open Find command and type part of the function name in the current interface language.
  2. Select a result and distinguish similar tasks, such as renaming versus writing metadata.
  3. Confirmation opens the same function as its main-menu item.

Custom shortcuts

Shortcut settings accept gestures such as Ctrl+Shift+J or F9. An empty value disables that assignment. Unmodified navigation keys are reserved. Resolve conflicts by changing the previous assignment first. Restoring defaults replaces custom changes. Invalid saved settings are not applied as a valid shortcut set. See standard keys.

Title: Media: choose a workflow
Summary: Conversions, editing, metadata and naming.
Body:
Quick image edits are part of the converter. Use the Size and rotation sidebar page for resizing and rotation; the mode, width, height and rotation controls stay on one row. Keep original format preserves each image format and extension, or each audio container and codec. Unchanged audio is stream-copied. Unsupported edits of an original codec report an error and leave the source intact.

Current workflow

Convert in the context menu of supported images/audio opens the converter. Concurrent files means complete independently converted files, not chunks of one file. Available CPU capacity is shared across workers. More workers than CPU threads may not improve speed. Percentages have a dedicated column; the footer shows weighted progress and estimated remaining time after an initial measurement. Estimates can change with pauses and throughput. Finishing includes validation and committing the output.

Media groups image, audio and naming commands. First decide whether to change actual format or content, image dimensions, filename or stored metadata.

  • Image conversion and resizing: new image outputs.
  • Audio conversion: codecs, bitrate, channels and streams.
  • Advanced options: stream copy, video, loudness and metadata.
  • Names and metadata: two opposite workflows.
  • Batch rename: names without format conversion.

Select Images or Convert audio in the converter. Filtering the queue does not delete the other type’s items. Conversion settings and Advanced preserve the same batch configuration. Destination and parallelism remain visible below both tabs.

Title: Linux disks: ext2, ext3 and ext4
Summary: Read files from physical USB disks and raw images without installing a Linux filesystem driver.
Body:
Open Commands → Disk tools → Linux disks. USB disks and the first disk’s partitions load automatically. Selecting another disk automatically reads its partitions. Choose Open left or Open right to select the destination panel. Refresh discovers connected disks again; Scan partitions repeats the selected disk scan.

Open a partition in a file panel

After scanning, choose Open left or Open right. Enter opens a directory and Backspace opens its parent. F3 prepares the file preview in the opposite panel. F5 copies the selection into a new Linux-export folder in the local opposite panel. The source is read-only: editing, rename, delete, move and paste are blocked. Use F5 instead of clipboard transfers or drag and drop.

Automatic discovery

When File Compass runs as administrator, background discovery finds supported EXT partitions on USB disks, including disks without Windows drive letters, and adds EXT entries to the drive selector. Device changes are checked about every ten seconds; partition scans are cached. Without administrator access use Commands → Disk tools → Linux disks and Open as administrator. A manual scan also reports unsupported and dirty partition errors.

Open a Linux disk

  1. Connect the USB disk. Cancel any Windows request to initialize or format it.
  2. Choose Commands → Disk tools → Linux disks. Refresh devices, select the physical USB disk and scan its partitions. A Windows drive letter is not required.
  3. If access is denied, use Open as administrator. A separate reader opens after the Windows permission prompt; select the disk again.
  4. Select a supported ext partition. Enter or double-click opens folders; Backspace goes up. The address field shows the Linux path.

Preview and copy

F3 previews one ordinary file up to 64 MiB. F5 copies selected files or folders into a new Linux-export folder inside your chosen destination. Existing destination files are never overwritten. Copying to the same physical source disk is refused. Cancel stops the reader process; completed copies remain and temporary partial files are removed where possible.

Symbolic links and special device files are skipped. Linux names differing only in case can collide on Windows; the first completed copy is retained and the other is reported. Reserved Windows names, unsupported characters and excessive directory depth are reported rather than silently renamed. Check the completed and skipped counts.

Supported sources and limits

The reader opens physical USB disks and raw disk or partition images. MBR and GPT partition tables are supported, including 512-byte and 4096-byte sectors. Use Open image for raw IMG, RAW, DD or ext images; compressed images and VHD containers must first be converted separately. This does not mount a drive in Explorer.

All source handles and filesystem streams are read-only. Dirty filesystems requiring journal recovery and unsupported ext features are refused. Safely unmount the disk in Linux; perform any filesystem check there. Encrypted LUKS, LVM logical volumes and RAID are not decoded by this reader. Btrfs and ZFS are not part of this feature.

USB removal and formatting

Right-click a confirmed removable USB drive in the drive bar to request safe removal or open the Windows format dialog. Removal concerns the physical USB device and all its volumes; Windows may refuse it while files are open. Formatting erases data and is a separate operation, never part of reading Linux files. System and application disks do not get these commands.

Flash drive icon and context menu

Removable flash drives use the standard Windows removable-drive icon in both the drive bar and the drive selector. Right-click the specific drive and choose Safe removal or Format. Format opens the original Windows dialog for that exact drive letter; erasing starts only when you confirm it there.

Before either action the application releases previews and moves affected panels to the system drive. Safe removal releases all drive letters on the same physical disk. Commands are disabled during active file operations. Windows can refuse removal when another program holds files open; close those files and retry. The application never forces removal or terminates another program. A confirmation appears after successful removal.

Title: Application and component updates
Summary: Version checks, verified downloads and component rollback.
Body:
Settings → Updates

Manual or daily checks show installed/available versions, source, path and errors. Daily checking does not download or install. Download update is a separate action with progress and cancellation.

Official sources

7-Zip and rclone use vendor releases; FFmpeg uses gyan.dev Windows builds linked by ffmpeg.org. smartmontools may require a manual workflow if its release lacks a verifiable SHA-256. Magick.NET / OpenMP, its native library and runtime are updated together with File Compass. The File Compass GitHub release address is not configured yet: application self-updating is prepared but inactive.

Safe activation

Packages are checked for SHA-256, architecture, exact files and functional version. Missing or mismatched verification blocks installation. Prepared components remain in profile data; shipped files are not overwritten. Loaded 7-Zip and rclone changes wait until restart. Apply prepared activates eligible packages; Restore previous schedules rollback. Component rollback does not replace user data. Historical packages are not deleted automatically.
